subject: AWS private offering — Datapulse: tiered rev-share + payment term ask

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@datapulse.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@datapulse.com
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer details

Thanks Aditya — quick recap from our side after the call this morning. Datapulse is evaluating a private listing on AWS and we'd like to confirm the commercial structure before we move to legal/procurement. Our asks: 

- Tiered rev-share: 25% first $200k, 20% next $300k, 12% thereafter (we proposed slightly different tiers during the demo).
- Marketplace listing fee waiver for the first 90 days.
- 12-month committed minimum (we can commit to $500k ARR annualized).
- Payment: net 90 (our standard), with netting allowed against AWS marketplace credits.

Would Redwood be able to support the above? We want to get a private listing live in Q3. Attaching an internal note.

Best,
Alex
VP Partnerships, Datapulse

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. We're excited to move forward. Quick notes from my side: 

- We can support tiered rev-share but need to align on netting mechanics and reporting cadence.

- Net 90 is outside standard marketplace terms for new private offers; finance will need assurance (credit / letters).

Next step: internal approval request and then a short redline MOU to Datapulse.

Subject: Fwd: AWS private listing — Datapulse asks (internal)

Team — forwarding Datapulse asks. Summary of deviations from standard private offer template: 

1) Tiered rev-share structure (25/20/12) vs. our standard single-split approach. Business rationale: large strategic customer, good reference potential.
2) Marketplace listing fee waiver (90 days). Operational impact: small, but needs product ops alignment.
3) Payment: net 90 and netting against AWS credits (finance exposure).
4) Commit: 12 months / $500k ARR minimum — positive for revenue visibility.

My recommendation: approve tiered rev-share and 90-day fee waiver, conditional on: 
- Finance signs off on credit terms with a letter of credit or upfront partial payment (net 90 only if credit check passes).
- Legal adds a simple clawback clause if usage doesn't meet minimum within quarter 2.
- Rev-share payout schedule to be monthly with detailed usage reporting to avoid reconciliation burdens.

Request: exec concurrence for non-standard rev-share and payment term deviation. This is time-sensitive — Datapulse wants to go live in Q3.

Thanks,
Aditya

Aditya — quick legal/ops read: 

- Net 90: strong risk. We need SOX/finance alignment and an approved credit memo (Naomi can confirm). If finance requires an LC or upfront 25% deposit, we should make that explicit.
- Fee waiver: ok but cap it to listing costs only; do not waive transactional or support fees. Add an expiry clause (90 days from live date).
- Tiered rev-share: acceptable if the tiers are dollar-driven and we can automate payout thresholds. Include an audit right and a mutual reconciliation cadence (monthly).
- Clawback: propose a 60-day clawback if minimums aren't met in successive quarters.

I'll draft the necessary clauses on the MOU and mark the redlines. Please confirm if we want to include a product acceptance window for the listing (prod vs. beta).

-Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
